GUIDELINES FOR SODIUM RESTRICTION
Salt substitutes containing potassium chloride should be 
recommended only if approved by a physician. Potassium is 
generally contraindicated for patients with renal disease. Salt-
free, herb-based seasoning products are readily available in 
most grocery stores and should be suggested instead.
•	 Instruct patients/clients on reading the Nutrition Facts food 
label for sodium content of foods.
•	 Encourage patients to prepare food at home without adding 
salt and to limit eating in restaurants.
•	 Recommend baked products, using sodium-free baking 
powder, potassium bicarbonate (instead of sodium bicarbon-
ate or baking soda), and salt-free shortening in place of those 
containing sodium.
•	 Avoid obviously salted foods such as bouillon, soup and 
gravy bases, canned soups and stews; bread and rolls with 
salt toppings, salted crackers; salted nuts or popcorn, potato 
chips, pretzels, and other salted snack foods. Avoid buying 
vegetables prepared in sauce.
•	 Avoid smoked or cured meats, such as bacon, bologna, cold 
cuts, other processed meats, chipped or corned beef, frank-
furters, ham, koshered or kosher style meats, and canned 
meat poultry.
•	 Avoid salted and smoked fish such as cod, herring, and 
sardines.
